The PEK extraction guard correctly tightened (needlessly blocking off-market work is a real cost); the staleness watchdog correctly stays wide. done.title: Cowork leader-lock falsely suppresses legitimate FIRE ticks — owner_session (pid+startupTs) not stable across gateway-proxied per-tick calls, so the own-held heartbeat re-claim path is structurally unreachable
done.note: CONFIRMED (was 'suspected' 08:15Z, CONFIRMED 08:46Z same window). Mechanism: leader-lock owner_session token = pid-<pid>-ts-<startupTs>, regenerated per process. Cowork FIRE ticks run as separate gateway-proxied calls -> each tick sees a different owner_session -> when it re-reads an ALIVE lock it claimed on a PRIOR tick, the own-held heartbeat branch (which matches on owner_session equality) never matches -> falls through to the peer-held branch -> silent suppression of a legitimate FIRE. Evidence: 08:15Z chef-intraday MATCHED but re-claim returned claimed=false (lock alive from 08:00:44Z, ttl 1800s) -> PEER-HELD -> silent exit, YET slot token cowork-slot:chef-intraday claimed=true (no real peer) = contradiction. 08:45Z chef-eod fired clean precisely BECAUSE the 08:00Z lock had expired >1800s (stolen:true) = clean fresh claim. So: alive-lock => false peer-held suppression; expired-lock => correct fire. Benign 2026-06-05 (08:15Z intraday already fired 07:16Z) but LATENT product risk: any FIRE landing within 1800s of a prior leader claim by the same logical leader is dropped. FIX DIRECTION: make leader identity STABLE across per-tick gateway calls (durable leader id persisted in the lock store / coordination.db, not a per-process pid+startupTs), OR have the heartbeat/re-claim path treat 'lock held by my own logical leader key' as own-held regardless of session token. ROUTE: PO to confirm owner — leader-lock lives in the cowork dispatcher + mcp-server task-lock tool (coordination.db); likely dev-mcp-server (task_claim/leader-lock) + cowork-flow skill. Kin FU-LOCKSTORE-EXPIRED-GC, FU-CHEF-MARKER-INFLOW. Detected by dev-team tick 2026-06-05T09:10Z from drained cowork heartbeats. | DONE+LIVE 2026-06-05T10:xxZ. Root cause PROVEN by architect spike (VERDICT A, brief docs/architecture-briefs/2026-06-05-leader-lock-false-peer-held-spike.md): NOT 'owner_session regenerated per gateway call' (that theory was false — SERVER_SESSION_ID is process-stable) but owner_session NOT DURABLE ACROSS PROCESS RESTART. mcp-server restarted 08:11:38Z (FDA-1 deploy) 654s after cowork-leader claimed 08:00:44Z (owner_session pid-1-ts-1780613414482); new process minted a new SERVER_SESSION_ID -> 08:15Z heartbeat UPDATE WHERE owner_session=<new> matched 0 rows -> ok=false -> false PEER-HELD silent suppression. So EVERY deploy/restart silently orphaned the cowork-leader lock for up to its 1800s TTL. FIX (both layers, live): (1) mcp-server 1b058f40 — releaseOrphanTask + new MCP tool task_force_release_orphan(task_id,owner_agent,orphan_threshold_seconds=600,min120): force-releases a held lock ONLY when heartbeat_age>threshold (stale/dead holder); a FRESH heartbeat (live peer) is NOT released -> preserves the 2026-06-02 dup-spawn discriminator (no double-leader window). 8 new tests RED->GREEN (AC-SL-6/7), tsc clean, mcp-server rebuilt 10:30:50Z (tool count 160->161), raw-probe confirmed callable {released:false,lock_not_found}. (2) cowork-flow d88045c1 — leader-lock.md Step 0b now: claimed=false -> heartbeat probe ok=false -> task_force_release_orphan; released=true -> re-claim & proceed (restart-orphan); released=false -> live peer, silent exit. 80L<120L cap.
